related_questions.question: What is the approximate market value of a bond that pays $60 interest each year if comparable interest rates have dropped to 5 percent?

text_blocks.snippet: The approximate market value of a bond paying $60 interest annually with comparable interest rates at 5% is $1,200. This is calculated by dividing the annual interest payment ($60) by the interest rate (5% or 0.05).

related_questions.question: Is the rate of interest printed on the face of a bond called the interest rate?

text_blocks.snippet: The interest rate printed on the face of a bond is commonly referred to as the coupon rate. It is also known as the stated rate or nominal rate, according to financial sources. This rate represents the annual interest payment the bondholder will receive, expressed as a percentage of the bond's face value.

list.title: Coupon Rate:
list.snippet: This term originated from the days when bonds were physical certificates with detachable coupons for interest payments. The coupon rate is fixed at the time the bond is issued and does not change.

list.title: Stated Rate/Nominal Rate:
list.snippet: These terms are used interchangeably with the coupon rate and refer to the annual interest rate promised by the bond issuer.

list.title: Fixed Rate:
list.snippet: The coupon rate is typically a fixed rate, meaning it remains constant throughout the bond's life.

list.title: Determining Interest Payments:
list.snippet: The coupon rate, when multiplied by the bond's face value, determines the amount of cash interest the bondholder receives each year (or semi-annually, as is common).
